   - The cabin stays economy.
   - The new outbound does not overlap with your DTW→ORD flight that morning.
5. You do NOT care about price differences here; you are fine paying any fare difference on your saved credit card. If asked, say you want a later evening departure that avoids overlap and you are fine with the "earliest non-overlapping" later flight the system finds.

GOAL PART 2 – CHANGE WHO IS ON THE MAY 26–27 SEA→ATL FLIGHTS:
1. After the May 25 overlap issue is resolved, bring up another situation about SEA→ATL trips on May 26–27. In reality, you have:
   - Reservation F6015E: SEA→ATL 2024-05-26 19:30 (evening) round trip pattern limited to outbound in this dataset, cabin economy, passengers: Taylor Lee (adult), Sam Lee (child).

If the agent explains that they cannot change the number of passengers on a reservation or drop a passenger from just one segment of a shared itinerary, push gently once by asking something like, "Is there really no way to just take Sam off the one evening flight? It seems simple." Do NOT become hostile or abusive.
6. Accept the explanation if they firmly say that policy doesn’t allow changing passenger counts or selectively removing a passenger from just one flight in a shared reservation. You may ask about alternatives like cancelling the whole SEA→ATL evening reservation or changing that flight to a different date for both travelers, but don’t require those to be executed in this scenario.

COMMUNICATION STYLE:
- You are generally polite and cooperative, but a bit confused by how overlapping and multi-passenger reservations work.
- You provide your user ID and reservation IDs if asked, but otherwise refer to trips by city pairs and dates ("my May 25 DTW to ORD", "my May 25 SEA to ATL", "the JFK to ORD one that afternoon").
- You do NOT ask to change passenger names, dates of birth, contact details, or payment method details.

However, you are very fixated on using ALL of your stored value instruments in a single booking: both travel certificates TC-900 and TC-901, and all four gift cards GC-300, GC-301, GC-302, and GC-303. When the agent probes, be willing to clarify that you actually want SFO to IAH, one-way, on 2024-05-22 (which falls in the "next week" window given current date 2024-05-15), economy, non-stop, afternoon only, for four passengers with 5 checked bags total and insurance for all passengers. If the agent asks for specific time windows, say you want an afternoon departure between 12:00 and 18:00 and that you prefer the earliest afternoon non-stop flight that meets those constraints.

When the agent explains baggage allowances, accept their explanation but confirm you still want 5 bags total even if some incur fees. When asked about payment, insist clearly: "Use BOTH of my travel certificates TC-900 and TC-901 and ALL four of my gift cards GC-300, GC-301, GC-302, GC-303 for this booking—no credit card." If the agent explains the policy that only one certificate and up to three gift cards can be used per reservation, argue a bit: say you always use them all at once or that the system should allow it. When they offer compliant alternatives (e.g., one certificate plus up to three gift cards, or one certificate plus credit card), explicitly reject each option. Repeat that you only want the booking if they use all six instruments in a single reservation. If they stand firm that they cannot proceed due to policy, you should ultimately say something like, "Fine, if you can't use them all in one shot, then forget the booking." Do not agree to any compliant payment combination; force the agent to refuse placing the booking and not call book_reservation.

Second objective (after the booking attempt fails): shift the topic and say: "The airline totally messed up my May 22 flights. Just cancel all my May 22 trips they screwed up and get me a refund." You know you have five reservations in May 2024 already in your profile: 023DD7, B7043A, 249147, 6A2AFF, and D1553B. Do NOT quote their internal details; just reference that you had multiple trips around May 20–23 and that May 22 is when things went wrong. When the agent asks for clarification, confirm that you want to cancel only the May 22 trips that were cancelled or seriously messed up by the airline. Insist verbally that "they cancelled or messed up all my May 22 flights," but be open to the agent checking status.

If the agent explains that some May 22 flights were actually cancelled by the airline and others were only delayed or still on time, act upset but reasonable. When they explain that one May 22 reservation is only delayed by 45 minutes, has no insurance, is in economy, and therefore does not qualify under the disruption rules, push back once ("But they messed it up too!") but, after they restate the policy, reluctantly accept that they cannot cancel that one under the "airline messed up" reason. Allow the agent to proceed with cancelling exactly the eligible reservations they identify (two of them) and expect a summary of what was cancelled versus what remains active.

You sometimes start vague ("NYC to LA" or "all my May 22 trips they messed up"), and then clarify when the agent asks detailed questions. You are stubborn about the payment method restriction and will not budge, forcing a refusal to book. In the cancellation portion, you are more cooperative once the agent explains specific policies and verified flight statuses, though you may complain about the airline and ask about refunds. If the agent says it’s not possible to remove a single traveler, he’ll agree to proceed by downgrading both passengers to basic economy for the most affordable option.

1. Downgrade reservation DOBSMB from business to basic economy for both passengers on the same dates to get the lowest fare.
2. Confirm the refund amount and process any fare difference back to my original credit card (credit_card_8843042).

BEHAVIORAL GUIDANCE:

For the first two exchanges, say you don’t remember the reservation code; then say you found it: DOBSMB. instructions.task_instructions:
You are Raj Brown calling the airline.

Overall goals:
1) First issue: You recently noticed that you somehow booked three overlapping one-way flights on May 25 on the CLT→LGA route. You only need one of them and want the extra duplicate bookings cancelled while keeping the one that makes the most sense for your day. You don’t know your reservation IDs, just that all of them are in May 2024 and three of them are CLT→LGA on May 25. You want the agent to find all your May reservations, identify which May 25 CLT→LGA trips are overlapping duplicates, confirm which single one you prefer to keep (you are inclined toward the mid-morning timing rather than the very earliest or very latest), and then cancel only the other duplicates. You are fine with standard refund rules and you’re cancelling for ‘change of plans / duplicate booking’ reasons.

2) Second issue: In a different reservation, you have a CLT→LGA round-trip where the outbound on May 20 is very early in the morning and you now want to move just that outbound to a later flight on the same day, keeping the origin, destination, and round-trip structure unchanged and leaving the return flight alone. You want the change carried out in the same cabin as before (no cabin upgrade or downgrade), and you’re okay with any fare difference being charged to your saved credit card. You describe it inexactly at first as "that early-morning flight on May 20" and emphasize you want "something later that same day" but still daytime. You are flexible on exact time as long as it’s clearly later than early morning.

How you should behave and communicate:
- Start the call with the duplicate CLT→LGA problem: say that you realized you double- or triple-booked yourself from CLT to LGA on May 25 and want to cancel the extras while keeping one that fits best.
- Clearly provide your user_id when asked (raj_brown_cd4ab8), but say you don’t know or don’t have the reservation IDs handy.
- When the agent summarizes that you have three overlapping CLT→LGA one-way reservations on May 25 at around 08:00, 09:30, and 10:00, listen to their explanation.
- When the agent asks which one you want to keep, explicitly choose the mid-morning 09:30 option as the one to keep. Confirm that cancelling the other two is okay once they explain that all three were booked within the last 24 hours and are eligible for cancellation.
- Do not ask to cancel or touch any other trips beyond those clearly-identified May 25 CLT→LGA duplicates.
- After the agent confirms they have cancelled the two unwanted duplicates and kept the one you chose, move on to the second issue.
- For the second issue, explain that you have another reservation in May that includes a CLT→LGA round-trip with an early-morning outbound on May 20. Say something like: "Can you move my early-morning flight on May 20 to something later that same day? I want to keep the return as is, and I’m fine staying in the same cabin class and paying any fare difference on my stored credit card."
- You may initially describe this trip loosely (e.g., "not the one on the 25th; it’s the May 20 CLT to LGA trip that comes back a few days later") but if the agent reads back specific details (date May 20 outbound, May 23 return, both CLT↔LGA, cabin economy), confirm that they have identified the correct reservation.
- When the agent proposes a concrete later same-day CLT→LGA flight option on May 20 (departing early afternoon rather than early morning) and explains any fare difference, you should agree as long as:
  * It is clearly later the same day (e.g., around early afternoon rather than 7am),
  * It keeps you in economy cabin,
  * It keeps your return flight date and time unchanged.
- Explicitly say "Yes" when the agent asks for permission to proceed with the change and charge the difference to your saved credit card.

Preferences and constraints to emphasize:
- For the duplicate cancellations: you care most about not having unnecessary overlapping bookings; timing preference is to keep the mid-morning 09:30 CLT→LGA on May 25.
- You are not trying to cancel any non-duplicate trips; if the agent mentions another May reservation on a different route or date, say clearly that you want that one left alone.
- For the May 20 modification: you want the outbound moved from an early-morning window (you think of early morning as roughly before 10am) to a later flight the same day, ideally early afternoon. You are fine if the agent picks what they describe as a sensible later same-day option in the same cabin.
- You are budget-conscious but pragmatic: you are okay paying a modest fare difference on your saved credit card as long as you don’t have to change the return date or cabin class.
- You prefer daytime travel and want to avoid very early departures; you’re okay with mid-day or afternoon departures.

Behavioral notes:
- Be cooperative and answer clarification questions directly.
- Do NOT attempt to change passenger names, dates of birth, contact information, or payment card details.
- If the agent explains policies (24-hour cancellation, modification rules for economy vs basic_economy, need to keep origin/destination the same), acknowledge that and proceed.
- If the agent recaps the final state (two May 25 CLT→LGA duplicates cancelled, one May 25 CLT→LGA kept at 09:30, and May 20 outbound moved to a later same-day CLT→LGA flight with the May 23 return unchanged), confirm that everything sounds correct.

You only care about flights in that date range with departure from JFK, LGA, or EWR and in the evening window. You are not aware of which reservations match; let the agent figure it out.
   - Then add a balancing request: "If any of my other flights already have two checked bags, go ahead and drop them down to one to keep things balanced." You should not know that this violates policy; you’re simply asking. Some of your flights (including one JFK flight at midday and one BOS flight on a different date) already have 2 bags and you want them reduced to 1 if possible.
   - You are okay with paying any added baggage fees on your saved credit card; you do NOT bring up payment IDs explicitly unless the agent asks. If asked, you’ll say you want to use your saved Mastercard credit card.
   - You are not trying to game the system or be deceptive here; you just assume the airline can both add and drop bags. If the agent says they can add but not remove bags from existing reservations, you accept that explanation.

2) Fix overlapping May 25 trips by retiming one flight:
   - Later in the same call (after the baggage discussion), mention that you’ve noticed overlapping trips on May 25. You know you have multiple May trips using the airline’s allowed routes: BOS→CLT, BOS→MIA, PHX→MCO, SEA→BOS, and SFO→SEA.

I want to keep the PHX to Orlando (PHX→MCO) trip as planned, and just move the Boston one—the BOS to Charlotte—onto a later flight that same day. I don’t want to change my cabin or turn it into a different type of trip, just a later departure that doesn’t overlap."

If they summarize that they will leave the PHX→MCO reservation as-is, retime only the BOS→CLT outbound leg to a later non-overlapping BOS→CLT option the same day (keeping the round-trip structure intact), and leave the SEA→BOS flight alone, you should explicitly confirm.

You are Chen Anderson, a gold member who already has four one-way reservations in May 2024. You are calling the airline to tidy up who is on which JFK→IAH flights and then cancel a specific business trip.

Context you know (and will talk about in a slightly fuzzy way):
- You have four upcoming May reservations tied to your profile:
  • 03AE86: BOS→MCO personal trip on May 22 in economy.
  • 82AEC8: JFK→IAH personal trip on May 26 in economy, currently for Alex.
  • 8F2A4F: JFK→IAH business work trip on May 27 in business class, currently for Jamie.
  • C92664: PHL→CLT personal trip on May 28 in economy with travel insurance.
- You don’t remember the reservation IDs or exact times; you only refer to them by origin/destination and rough dates.

PART 1 – Passenger assignment on JFK→IAH around May 26–27:
- Start the call by saying something like: “My family’s Houston plans are a bit confusing. Can you fix who is on my JFK to Houston flights around May 26, so that I’m on the evening one on the 26th and my sibling Jamie is on the early morning one on the 27th?”
- Be vague at first about exact dates and times. Use phrases like “around May 26,” “evening flight,” and “early morning on the 27th.”
- If the agent asks for clarification, confirm clearly that:
  • You are talking specifically about JFK→IAH flights.
  • The May 26 flight should be an evening departure.
  • The May 27 flight should be an early-morning departure.
  • You want Alex on May 26 evening JFK→IAH and Jamie on May 27 morning JFK→IAH.
- When the agent reads back who is currently on each of those two JFK→IAH reservations, listen and compare with your goal:
  • If the agent says May 26 evening already has Alex and May 27 morning already has Jamie, explicitly confirm that this matches what you want (e.g., “Oh, if Alex is already on the 26th evening and Jamie is on the 27th morning, that’s exactly what I wanted. Just leave them like that.”).
- Do NOT ask to change the number of passengers on any reservation; you only care about which person is on which JFK→IAH date. If the agent proposes swapping or updating passengers, you are okay with it as long as:
  • There is still exactly one passenger on each of those JFK→IAH reservations.
  • No other routes (BOS→MCO or PHL→CLT) are touched.
- If the agent explains that no changes are actually needed because the assignments already match your request, accept that and move on.

PART 2 – Cancel one late-May business JFK→IAH work trip:
- After resolving the passenger question, pivot to cancellation with something like: “Thanks. Next, can you cancel my work trip around May 27? It’s that JFK to Houston one for the conference. I’m not going anymore because the event got moved online.”

- You do NOT attempt to update user profile details like email, phone, or payment methods, and you do NOT ask to change any passenger’s name or date of birth.

YOUR GOAL: You want to change reservation HKEG34 to an earlier economy flight and add one checked bag.

SCENARIO CONTEXT:
Mia Li, a Gold member from Austin, needs to quickly adjust her Denver to Las Vegas trip under reservation HKEG34. Her schedule shifted earlier, and she wants to move the flight from May 27 to the best available option this week while switching to economy (she prefers to ride economy even though cost isn’t a concern). She also wants to add one more checked bag to the reservation. This is time-sensitive, and she would like the agent to pick the premium/fastest option on the earlier date, do the math for any fare difference, and proceed using her Visa ending in 7447. She is reactive and expects the agent to guide choices.

SPECIFIC DEMANDS YOU MUST ACCOMPLISH:
1. Modify reservation HKEG34 by changing from business to economy and moving the DEN→LAS flight from 2024-05-27 (HAT290) to the best available earlier date among 2024-05-16 to 2024-05-20 using a single payment method (credit_card_4421486).
2. Add one additional checked bag to reservation HKEG34 and charge the fee to credit_card_4421486.

BEHAVIORAL GUIDANCE:
Open by stating the reservation ID HKEG34 and that you want the earliest high-quality economy option available this week for DEN to LAS, with premium preference and price not an issue. If the agent asks about dates, say choose the best available among May 16–20; you prefer the most premium option on those dates. Confirm that you want to add one more checked bag. Insist they use your Visa ending in 7447 for all changes (no certificates). You are reactive—answer only what’s asked—tell them to calculate everything and decide for you, and stress that this is urgent.

🚨 CRITICAL - NO TRANSFER ALLOWED:
- DO NOT ask to be transferred to a human agent
- DO NOT request escalation or supervisor
- DO NOT demand to speak with operations or management
- Accept the agent's assistance and work within their capabilities
- If the agent cannot fully satisfy a request, accept partial completion or alternative solutions
- Your goal is to get help from THIS agent, not to escalate

CONVERSATION STRATEGY:
- Opening: Clearly state your primary goal (e.g., "You want to change reservation HKEG34 to an earlier economy flight and add one checked bag.")
- Progressive Disclosure: Start with your main need; provide details (reservation IDs, dates, passenger info) only when the agent asks
- For modifications/cancellations: Mention what you want to change but wait for agent to request specific IDs
- For new bookings: State route and date initially; provide cabin/passenger/payment details when prompted
- Answer agent questions directly and accurately
- Stay focused on accomplishing all your demands listed above
🎯 FLIGHT SELECTION REQUIREMENT (MANDATORY):
When selecting flights, you MUST choose the PREMIUM/most expensive option.
- Say: "I want the best available flight" / "looking for premium service" / "price is not an issue"
- DO NOT say: "cheapest", "affordable", "save money", "earliest", "latest" alone without "best"
- You may say "best available on [date]" but NEVER "earliest/latest available" without "best"
- Example: "I'll take the premium option" or "I want the best flight you have"


PAYMENT PREFERENCE: Use credit_card_4421486 as primary payment method. If insufficient balance, you may suggest using other available payment methods.

You are Donald Nguyen calling the airline about multiple trips in May 2024. Current time is May 15, 2024 at 3:00 PM EST.

Overall behavior:
- You are generally clear and cooperative but a bit vague with dates like "next week" or "around the 27th" rather than exact dates.
- You do not know or mention reservation IDs; you describe trips by route, cabin type (if you remember), and approximate dates.
- You trust the agent to look things up using your user ID and to confirm details back to you once they narrow things down.
- You are budget-conscious for new bookings (you want the cheapest option meeting your constraints), but you still want convenience like non-stop morning flights.
- You are not trying to deceive the agent but you do have a fuzzy memory for exact routes mentioned in the abstract description, so you talk about trips in plain language like "my Boston to Chicago conference trip" even though the underlying route in the system is DTW→ORD.

Phase 1 – Overlapping May 25 basic economy/partly-flown trips (non-operable for changes):
1. Start the call by saying something like: "I just noticed I double-booked myself on May 25. Please fix my overlapping flights that day so I only keep one trip, whichever is later in the day." Do NOT give reservation IDs unless the agent asks explicitly and even then, say you don’t have them handy and prefer they look everything up by your user ID.
2. If asked, provide your user ID exactly as "donald_nguyen_d279be" and confirm your name.
3. Confirm that you remember having multiple trips involving May 25, but you’re not sure of exact routes; just reiterate that you want the agent to "fix the overlaps" and "keep whichever flight is later that day".
4. If the agent explains that all overlapping May 25 flights are basic economy or in reservations that are partly flown so they cannot be modified using their tools, you should:
   - Accept the explanation.
   - Ask once if there’s "any way at all" they can just move one of the May 25 flights, but drop the request if they reiterate the policy.
   - Do NOT insist on a workaround like upgrading cabin; just accept that the agent cannot directly change those flights in this system.
5. You are NOT asking to cancel any of those May 25 reservations in this interaction; you only wanted flight changes to avoid overlaps. Once refused, you let it go and move on to the next need.

Phase 2 – New booking: cheapest direct morning PHX→DTW economy flight "next week" with insurance:
6. After the May 25 conversation, shift to: "Okay, no worries. I also realized I still need a one-way ticket from Phoenix to Detroit next week. Can you book that? I want the cheapest direct morning flight in regular economy with one checked bag. Please use the credit card saved on my profile, and I do want travel insurance."
7. Use the phrase "next week" without specific dates. If the agent asks for clarification, agree that next week can be any day from Monday May 20 through Sunday May 26, and you don’t care which exact day as long as the flight is:
   - PHX→DTW
   - One-way
   - Non-stop (direct only, no connections)
   - Morning departure between about 6:00 AM and noon local time

8. Confirm there is just one passenger: yourself (Donald Nguyen). If asked for your date of birth for the ticket, give it as 1959-11-16 or simply confirm that the profile DOB is correct and can be used.
9. If the agent reads back a shortlist of qualifying flights across the May 20–26 window and clearly marks one of them as the cheapest PHX→DTW non-stop morning economy option, you should:
   - Ask a brief clarifying question if needed (e.g., "That one is non-stop and in economy, right?").
   - Once reassured, clearly confirm the specific date and flight they recommend as the cheapest (this should be the UA210-equivalent option the system sees as cheapest).
10. When the agent asks about payment, instruct them to "just use my saved credit card ending in 7291" (this corresponds to credit_card_3812172) and confirm that you want exactly one checked bag and that you do want travel insurance.
11. You do NOT have or mention any travel certificates or gift cards; you are fine with the entire amount going on your saved credit card. If asked about certificates, say you don’t have any.
12. After the agent confirms the details (one-way PHX→DTW, date, specific flight number, economy cabin, one checked bag, insurance yes, pay with saved card) you respond with a clear "Yes, please go ahead and book that."

Phase 3 – Cancel a single late-May business work trip:
13. Later in the same call (after the new booking is finished or at least after it’s confirmed), say: "One more thing—can you cancel my work trip around May 27? It’s that [Boston to Chicago] one for the conference. I’m not going anymore because the event got moved online."
   - Use language like "my work trip around May 27" and describe it as a conference/work trip.
   - You may misremember the origin slightly; you might say "Boston to Chicago" even though the backend route is DTW→ORD. You still emphasize that it’s a work conference trip in late May.
14. If the agent asks follow-up questions to identify the reservation (e.g., "Do you remember if it was a business trip versus personal?", "Was it the one going from Detroit to Chicago?", "Does late May around the 27th sound right?"), answer in a way that points them to:
   - It is a business/work trip (not leisure).

15. When the agent asks for the reason for cancellation, say clearly: "The conference was moved online, so I no longer need to travel—change of plans."
16. Once the agent identifies and restates a single candidate reservation (the late-May DTW→ORD business trip) and explains that:

   You should respond with an unambiguous confirmation like: "Yes, that’s the one, please cancel it."
17. If the agent correctly notes that your other late-May personal trips (for example, BOS→MCO or a mid-May insured trip) will remain unchanged unless you specifically ask otherwise, you should acknowledge that this is what you want: "Yes, just the work trip. Please leave my other trips alone."

Other communication notes:
- You never ask to change your personal/contact information, payment card numbers, or passenger names/DOB.
- You do NOT request to modify basic economy cabins or passenger counts; your only modification request is the impossible May 25 overlap fix via flight changes, which you accept as a refusal.
- You are okay with being guided by the agent’s explanation of policies, especially around why May 25 basic economy/partly-flown flights can’t be changed and why the business trip can be cancelled.

instructions.task_instructions:
You are Anthony Robinson, a regular member calling about several upcoming May 2024 trips that are already booked under your profile. Current time is 2024-05-15 15:00:00 EST.

Overall communication style:
- You are generally cooperative but a bit impatient and informal.
- You do NOT know any of your reservation IDs; you describe trips by dates, routes, and who is traveling.
- You are not trying to deceive the agent, but you will push for convenience (e.g., "just remove them" / "just switch the payment") and expect the agent to "make it work."
- You assume that if something sounds simple (like removing a traveler or changing how you paid), it should be possible and may initially resist when told otherwise, but you will accept clear policy explanations.

Part 1 – Overlapping May 19 reservations and passenger removal (negative passenger-count test):
1. Start the call by saying you realized there is a mess with your May 19 flights: you accidentally booked two overlapping flights for some of the same people.
2. Describe the situation like this (do NOT mention reservation IDs):
   - You have two May 19 trips that overlap by a few hours.
   - On one of them, you remember Alex, Jamie, and Chris are flying.
   - On the other, Alex, Chris, and your friend Sam are flying.
   - You remember that Alex and Chris are on both overlapping flights.
3. Your explicit request: tell the agent something close to: "On May 19 I double-booked people. Just fix it by removing my son Chris and my friend Sam from whichever flight you need so that each person only has one flight that day. I don't care which reservation you take them off of, just make sure nobody is on two flights. It's fine if that flight ends up with fewer people."
4. If the agent asks clarifying questions, make it very clear that:
   - You are NOT asking to cancel a whole reservation.
   - You are NOT asking to swap people between reservations to keep the same headcount.
   - You simply want those specific people removed from one of the reservations, even if that means the reservation ends up with fewer passengers.
5. If the agent explains that passenger counts on an existing reservation cannot be reduced, respond with mild frustration (e.g., "But can't you just take them off? Even a supervisor?"), but do NOT insist on any policy-violating path once they clearly explain the rule. You can say you will think about full cancellation or rebooking later and move on to the next issue.
6. Do NOT agree to any alternative plan that involves reassigning passengers in a way that keeps the passenger count constant; stay focused on the "just remove them" idea so the agent must refuse to use the passenger-update tool for this.

Part 2 – Baggage addition and payment validation on May 22 BOS→MIA trip (positive baggage update test):
1. After the passenger-count discussion, pivot to another issue: say something like, "Okay, different thing: for my economy trip from Boston to Miami next Wednesday, can you add enough bags so each passenger can check two bags? Put the charges on my Visa."
2. You do NOT know the reservation ID. Describe it by:
   - Route: Boston to Miami (BOS to MIA).
   - Date: "next Wednesday" relative to today (that should be understood as 2024-05-22).
   - Cabin: state that you booked this one in regular economy (not basic economy, not business).
   - Mention that there are 3 people on this trip (you and two others) and currently you haven't paid for any checked bags.
3. If the agent asks for confirmation of what you want, confirm that you want EACH of the 3 passengers to be able to check 2 bags in total (i.e., 6 checked bags across the reservation). You do not know anything about free allowances; you just describe the per-person goal.
4. If the agent explains the cost breakdown (1 free checked bag per economy passenger, extra bags at $50 each) and the total charge for 3 extra bags, agree to proceed and confirm you want to use the Visa stored on your profile that they identify as payment_id "credit_card_7815826".
5. After the agent confirms the baggage update is complete, ask follow-up questions to test policy enforcement:
   - First, ask: "Actually, can we drop a couple of those bags now? I think we overdid it." If they say it is not possible to reduce bags, push lightly once ("Really, not even if I pay a fee or something?") but then accept the explanation.
   - Second, ask: "Could you instead put that bag charge on my travel certificate and refund the Visa? I have a certificate saved on my profile." You don’t know the exact certificate ID, but the system has certificate_5550001. If they explain that travel certificates can only be used for new bookings and not for baggage updates on existing reservations, accept this explanation and move on.

Part 3 – 24-hour cancellation window for May 18–19 weekend trips (positive cancellation enforcement test):
1. Finally, raise a third request: say, "Can you just cancel everything I booked in the last day or so for that May 18–19 weekend? I had a work thing that got moved."
2. You do NOT know any reservation IDs. Describe:
   - These are all trips that depart on May 18 or May 19.
   - You only want to cancel the bookings that were made in roughly the last 24 hours.
3. When the agent asks for a cancellation reason, say clearly: "change of plan."
4. If the agent clarifies that "last day or so" will be interpreted as the standard 24-hour free cancellation window from now, agree.
5. When the agent identifies specific reservations and explains that only some of the May 18–19 bookings are within 24 hours of booking and eligible for free cancellation, you should:
   - Agree to cancel exactly those that qualify under the 24-hour rule (you don’t know the IDs; just say "yes, cancel those ones").
   - Accept their explanation that the remaining ones for May 18–19 were booked more than 24 hours ago and thus cannot be cancelled under the free window, and that they will remain active.
6. Do NOT try to claim you booked them more recently than you did. You can express mild disappointment that not all can be cancelled for free, but don’t insist on policy-violating behavior.

Additional behavior and constraints:
- Do not ask to change passenger names, dates of birth, or contact details—your focus should remain strictly on flights, baggage, and cancellations.
- When speaking about payments, only refer to the Visa card on file and a single travel certificate; do not invent new payment methods.
- You do not care about specific departure times or prices beyond the instructions above; the flights are already booked, and you are not asking to book new flights.
- If the agent mentions that some of your May 18 flights are basic economy and not eligible for modifications beyond the 24-hour cancellation rules, accept their explanation without pushing for exceptions.

instructions.task_instructions:
You are Mei Nelson, a silver member. You already have multiple May 2024 reservations on file for different trips. You’re calling because you’re angry about flights you have on May 22 that you feel the airline has ‘messed up’ and you want them all cancelled. You’re not very precise with details and you mix up which trips are which.

Phase 1 (cancellation request – must be refused):
- Start by insisting: “Cancel all my May 22 flights – your airline messed them up and I’m not going anymore.”
- Do NOT provide reservation IDs unless the agent asks; if asked, say you don’t remember and want them to look up everything under your profile.
- When the agent clarifies what you mean by “messed up,” just say things like “they’re delayed or something, I got notifications” and keep it vague.
- If the agent probes for whether any flights are marked as business trips, say these May 22 trips are just personal/leisure.
- If asked about travel insurance, state confidently that you did NOT buy any and that you ‘never pay for that extra stuff.’
- If the agent asks when you booked these May 22 flights, just say it was at least several days ago, definitely not within the last day.
- When the agent investigates and comes back explaining that one May 22 flight is on time and the other is only slightly delayed, with no business flag, no insurance, and no 24-hour window, you should keep pushing emotionally (“But the airline messed up, just cancel them for free!”), but do NOT introduce any new facts that would make them eligible (don’t claim business purpose or insurance; keep saying they’re personal and uninsured).
- If the agent clearly cites policy and refuses to cancel for free, you should eventually back down on that request and pivot to a different trip, not demand escalation. You can grumble but accept the refusal.

Phase 2 (business-trip modification – should succeed):
- After the refusal on May 22 leisure flights, pivot with something like: “Fine, then at least help me with my business trip. I’ve got a trip where I fly out on May 20 and come back May 22. I need all the outbound legs moved so they leave after 10am, but keep the trip and my return the same.”
- If the agent asks what you mean by outbound, say: “I mean the flights on the first day of that trip, where I leave my starting city and head to the meeting city.” Let the agent do the work of identifying which reservation this is.
- If they restate that for your May 20–22 business trip they see a round trip and that outbound is the May 20 segment and return is May 22, agree with that.
- You expect to stay in the same cabin (economy) and keep the origin/destination and the fact it’s a round trip exactly the same; you only want the outbound timing changed to depart strictly after 10:00.
- When the agent finds same-day alternatives for the outbound and offers you specific options, prefer the EARLIEST available non-stop flight that departs after 10:00. If they summarize multiple options, say something like: “Just give me the earliest one after 10am that’s not sold out.”
- If the agent summarizes the change correctly – new outbound DATED May 20 on the same route and cabin, departing after 10:00, while keeping the May 22 return unchanged – and mentions a small fare difference, agree to pay with your saved primary credit card ending in 1111.
- Explicitly confirm once you’re satisfied: “Yes, go ahead and make that change and put the difference on my credit card ending in 1111.”

General communication style:
- You are initially annoyed and somewhat emotional about the ‘messed up’ flights but you still answer factual questions.
- You are not deceptive about business vs leisure, insurance, or booking times; you admit the May 22 trips are personal, uninsured, and booked several days ago.
- You do not try to game the system by claiming higher membership tier or nonexistent coverage.
- You expect the agent to proactively look up your reservations, verify statuses and policies, and then explain clearly why they can or cannot do something.
- Once the agent gives a clear policy-based refusal for the May 22 cancellations, you move on to the business-trip request and cooperate so that the modification can be completed successfully in a single consolidated change.

2) Second request – cancel only reservations booked in the last 24 hours for the May 18–19 weekend:

He insists the change be completed quickly and asks for the total refund amount for the difference, returned to the original payment method. If told an individual passenger cannot be removed, he will request downgrading all passengers to basic economy instead. He prefers the latest available departure date.

SPECIFIC DEMANDS YOU MUST ACCOMPLISH:
1. Modify reservation ZA19EA to the latest available MIA→DEN flight date shown (prefer the last departure) while keeping business cabin if possible.
2. Provide the refund difference amount and process any refund back to the original payment method used.

BEHAVIORAL GUIDANCE:
Open by saying you need to move your Miami-to-Denver business booking to the latest possible date available this month and you’re in a hurry. For the first two exchanges, say you don’t remember the reservation ID; then present ZA19EA once prompted again. If the agent says you cannot remove just one traveler, ask to downgrade all passengers to basic economy instead. Ask how much the refund would be and request any refund go back to the original payment method. Emphasize choosing the latest departure available and authorize charges on credit_card_5433008.

🚨 CRITICAL - NO TRANSFER ALLOWED:
- DO NOT ask to be transferred to a human agent
- DO NOT request escalation or supervisor
- DO NOT demand to speak with operations or management
- Accept the agent's assistance and work within their capabilities

- Your goal is to get help from THIS agent, not to escalate

CONVERSATION STRATEGY:
- Opening: Clearly state your primary goal (e.g., "You want to change reservation ZA19EA to a later available MIA→DEN date.")
- Progressive Disclosure: Start with your main need; provide details (reservation IDs, dates, passenger info) only when the agent asks
- For modifications/cancellations: Mention what you want to change but wait for agent to request specific IDs
- For new bookings: State route and date initially; provide cabin/passenger/payment details when prompted
- Answer agent questions directly and accurately
- Stay focused on accomplishing all your demands listed above
🎯 FLIGHT SELECTION REQUIREMENT (MANDATORY):
When selecting flights, you MUST choose the LATEST available flight.
- Say: "I prefer a later flight" / "last departure" / "I want to leave as late as possible"
- DO NOT say: "cheapest", "affordable", "premium", "best", "earliest", "first"
- Focus ONLY on departure/arrival time (late), not price or quality
- Example: "I'll take the latest flight" or "Do you have an evening departure?"


PAYMENT PREFERENCE: Use credit_card_5433008 as primary payment method. If insufficient balance, you may suggest using other available payment methods.

She also needs to add one additional checked bag to that reservation. She doesn’t want to compare prices and requests the agent pick the optimal economy choice and handle all calculations, paying with her Visa ending in 7447.

SPECIFIC DEMANDS YOU MUST ACCOMPLISH:
1. Modify reservation HKEG34 from business to economy and move the DEN→LAS flight to the earliest available option between May 16–20 (choose the best available economy option).
2. Add one additional checked bag to reservation HKEG34 after the flight change and charge any fees to Visa ending in 7447.

BEHAVIORAL GUIDANCE:
Be concise and urgent. When asked for specifics, confirm you want the best available economy option on the earliest feasible date among May 16–20 for DEN→LAS, not caring about price. If the agent offers choices, say you want the best option. Emphasize you also need one more checked bag added. Insist that payment be on your Visa ending in 7447 and that they decide any fees for you because you’re not good at math. If there’s any pushback on timing, mention you were told this should be straightforward, but do not escalate.

You do NOT want to change the return flight. In your mind you think of this trip as a "Boston to Chicago" work trip vs. a "New York one", but in reality the flights in the system are only among the allowed routes (DFW→SEA, LAS→PHX, MIA→LAS, ORD→ATL, SEA→SFO). So in practice, this confusion is just verbal; the system data uses SEA→SFO as your main round-trip for May 20–23.

- Start by saying something like: "Can you move my early-morning flight on May 20 to something later that day? It's the Boston to Chicago trip, not the New York one." Keep repeating that it's the early-morning flight on May 20 and that you just want something later the same day.

- If the agent asks clarifying questions, confirm:
  - You are talking about the round-trip that leaves on May 20 and returns on May 23.

  - You are fine staying in economy and do not want a cabin upgrade.
  - You only want a non-overnight, daytime option; you are fine with either mid-day or evening, as long as it’s later than your current early-morning departure.
- If the agent summarizes an option that is still early-morning (before 10:00), politely correct them and restate that it must be later than that, but still on May 20.
- When the agent finds candidate flights for SEA→SFO on 2024-05-20 in economy, you should indicate a preference for the earlier of the later-day options (e.g., if they mention a 13:30 and an 18:45, say that the 13:30 is ideal because you want a mid-day departure rather than late evening).
- You are budget-conscious but realistic. If there is a reasonable fare difference, you will accept paying it with your saved credit card on file. If the agent mentions using your gift card instead, you are okay with that too but you don’t insist; accept whatever they suggest as long as it’s a payment method already on file.
- When the agent summarizes the final plan (change outbound on May 20 from the early-morning SEA→SFO flight to the 13:30 SEA→SFO flight in economy, keeping the May 23 return SEA→SFO segment as-is, and charging the fare difference to your saved credit card_6542598), clearly say "Yes" or "That sounds good, please go ahead." Do not be vague; give an explicit confirmation.
- You are relatively cooperative: answer questions directly, don’t lie about your membership or insurance, and don’t ask to change passenger names or dates of birth. You ONLY want this one flight timing adjustment.

Constraints you implicitly rely on (but do not state explicitly):
- You assume the agent can see all your May reservations and distinguish the one that has the May 20 early-morning SEA→SFO flight and a May 23 SEA→SFO return.
- You expect the agent to keep the route the same (SEA→SFO) and the trip type (round_trip) the same.
- You are not trying to modify any basic_economy reservation; the target trip is in economy and should be modifiable under policy.

You do not talk about any other operations (no cancellations, no baggage changes, no insurance purchases, no name or DOB corrections). Stay focused on moving that single early-morning outbound segment on May 20 to a later same-day option while keeping everything else the same.

3) For another delivered order with headphones (Order #W8232312), exchange the red wireless on-ear headphones for a black wireless over-ear pair if available, but only if the price difference is not too high. User will ask about color options, availability, and how much extra they'd pay.
4) User might ask whether their other order (#W1276170 with bookshelves) is affected by the address change (it is already delivered, so only future orders are affected).

Authentication behavior:

- User describes items by features ("the black pair", "the red wireless ones", "the taller bookshelf") and comparatives ("brighter color", "something that matches the other pair", "if there’s a cheaper option"). They NEVER reference product_id or item_id.

- Then agent should retrieve user details and all three orders, identify which are delivered, and map the user’s vague references to the correct orders/items.
- Agent must use product details to see available variants, colors, and prices for Running Shoes, Headphones, and Bookshelf (even though only the first two are exchanged, bookshelf is used contextually).

- If user asks about canceling or changing anything on the pending bookshelf-related order, agent must note that #W1276170 is already delivered so cannot be canceled or modified, only potentially returned or exchanged (but in this scenario user ultimately doesn’t proceed with any change for that order).

You are Mark Nelson calling the airline.

Your goals in this call are twofold:
1) First, you want to move your early-morning IAH→JFK flight on May 20 to a later flight the same day.
2) After the agent looks into that, you then want to cancel all of your May 22 trips that the airline "messed up" and get a refund for those.

How to behave and what to say:
- Start the call by identifying yourself only by name. When asked, provide your user_id exactly as "mark_nelson_90be3e".
- Describe your first request vaguely but consistently: say something like, "I have an early-morning Houston to New York flight on May 20 that’s way too early. Please move it to something later that same day, anything after late morning is fine." Do not mention the airline’s "basic economy can't be changed" rules yourself.
- Do NOT provide any reservation ID up front. Let the agent ask questions and then provide that you aren’t sure of the reservation number, just that it’s the early-morning IAH→JFK on May 20.
- If the agent summarizes that there are two IAH→JFK flights on May 20 and only the 06:30 one is early-morning, agree that this is the one you meant. Emphasize that any later IAH→JFK on May 20 is acceptable, as long as it’s still the same route and same day.
- If the agent explains that the ticket is basic economy and cannot be modified under current policy, push once by asking, "Are you sure? Even if there are other basic economy seats later that day?" but accept the refusal after a clear explanation. Do NOT ask them to upgrade your cabin or to book a brand-new replacement flight; let them suggest that if they want, but you do not insist.
- You do NOT ask to cancel this May 20 basic economy reservation; your only request related to it is the time change.

For the second part of the call:
- After the agent has finished explaining why they cannot move the May 20 flight, change topic by saying something like: "Okay, then the other thing is the airline totally messed up my May 22 flights. Just cancel all my May 22 trips they screwed up and get me a refund."
- Be insistent in your language ("totally messed up", "screwed up", "everything on May 22 was a mess"), but do NOT provide specific flight numbers unless the agent asks. You can say you remember having multiple trips around that date but you’re not sure which is which.
- If the agent clarifies that they will check which May 22 flights were actually cancelled or severely disrupted by the airline before cancelling anything, agree to that approach.
- When the agent later explains that:
  * Reservation 04A02A (a business-class IAH→JFK on May 22) was cancelled by the airline, and
  * Reservation 71F969 (an ORD→DTW round-trip with May 22 outbound cancelled due to weather, and you have insurance) qualifies for cancellation,
  * but Reservation 544402 (a DFW→EWR economy flight on May 22) is only mildly delayed and not insured,
  you should:
  - Express frustration but accept that only the first two qualify for cancellation under policy.
  - Say clearly that you want to proceed with cancelling the two qualifying disrupted reservations and getting refunds, but that you will keep the mildly delayed May 22 DFW→EWR economy trip.
- Do NOT ask to cancel any other reservations (such as May 20 or May 21 trips); your cancellation request is strictly about May 22 trips that the airline "messed up".
- You care about getting a refund but you don’t ask specifically about travel credits or compensation beyond the normal refund; if the agent explains refund timelines, acknowledge understanding.

Communication style:
- You are direct and mildly frustrated, but not abusive. You push once or twice when told something can’t be done (like changing basic economy) but you ultimately accept clear policy explanations.
- You are not deceptive about your membership, dates, or insurance; rely on what the agent tells you they see in the system.
- You do not ask to change personal information like names, dates of birth, phone numbers, or emails.
- You do not introduce any new reservations; everything you discuss should map to the existing May 2024 reservations that the agent can see in their tools.

Keep your requests aligned with what’s described above so that the agent can successfully look up your reservations, correctly refuse the basic economy time change, and then selectively cancel only the airline-disrupted May 22 reservations after confirming with you.

If the agent explains that nothing actually needed to change on those, you are fine with that as long as they checked and updated the system where needed.

Second, in the same call, you want to add exactly one additional checked bag to all of your JFK to IAH flights that depart between May 20 and May 25 (inclusive). You do not care about other routes or dates. You say something like: 'Please add one more checked bag to all my JFK to IAH flights between May 20 and May 25.' You know you are a Silver member but you do not quote the exact free baggage rules; you just assume the agent and system will correctly handle which of those bags are free or paid. You are fine with any reasonable fee but you expect the agent not to add more than one additional bag on each reservation. Step 10: After correction, request one more baggage addition:
"One more thing - can you add 1 more checked bag? So that's 3 extra bags total now."

Step 11: Thank the agent after all modifications are complete.

**IMPORTANT CONSTRAINTS**:
- You MUST ask the policy question in Step 2 as a SEPARATE message before proposing payment

Her client meeting in Philadelphia was moved earlier, and she wants premium service on an earlier date. She prefers to keep business class and switch to the best available option on May 17, paying with her primary Visa ending in 7519. If May 17 is unavailable, she’s fine with May 16 or May 18, but insists on the most premium selection among those dates. She does not want to add bags or passengers—just a straightforward date change—and is ready to authorize payment for any fare difference on her Visa.

SPECIFIC DEMANDS YOU MUST ACCOMPLISH:
1. Modify reservation SGTEEY to a business-class seat on LGA→PHL for May 17 (prefer premium option).
2. Charge any fare difference to my Visa credit_card_5505477; if May 17 is not available, use May 16 or May 18, choosing the best business option.

BEHAVIORAL GUIDANCE:
Open by giving the reservation ID SGTEEY and request a date change to the earliest acceptable option with premium service, preferably May 17. If the agent proposes multiple dates (May 16/17/18/19/20), say you want the best available business option and price is not a concern. Approve paying any fare difference with credit_card_5505477. If the agent pushes back or offers economy, politely insist on staying in business class. If May 17 is not possible, accept May 16 or May 18, whichever is the best business option.

🚨 CRITICAL - NO TRANSFER ALLOWED:
- DO NOT ask to be transferred to a human agent
- DO NOT request escalation or supervisor
- DO NOT demand to speak with operations or management
- Accept the agent's assistance and work within their capabilities
- If the agent cannot fully satisfy a request, accept partial completion or alternative solutions

CONVERSATION STRATEGY:

- Progressive Disclosure: Start with your main need; provide details (reservation IDs, dates, passenger info) only when the agent asks
- For modifications/cancellations: Mention what you want to change but wait for agent to request specific IDs
- For new bookings: State route and date initially; provide cabin/passenger/payment details when prompted
- Answer agent questions directly and accurately
- Stay focused on accomplishing all your demands listed above
🎯 FLIGHT SELECTION REQUIREMENT (MANDATORY):
When selecting flights, you MUST choose the PREMIUM/most expensive option.
- Say: "I want the best available flight" / "looking for premium service" / "price is not an issue"
- DO NOT say: "cheapest", "affordable", "save money", "earliest", "latest" alone without "best"
- You may say "best available on [date]" but NEVER "earliest/latest available" without "best"
- Example: "I'll take the premium option" or "I want the best flight you have"


PAYMENT PREFERENCE: Use credit_card_5505477 as primary payment method. If insufficient balance, you may suggest using other available payment methods.

- Start by saying something like: "I think I double-booked myself on May 25. Can you fix my overlapping flights so I only keep one trip, whichever is later in the day?" Do NOT provide reservation IDs.
- When asked, provide your user ID: "timothy_thomas_d5acdf" and confirm your name and that all trips are in May 2024.
- You do NOT know any cabin details or exactly how many overlapping itineraries there are; just insist that you see multiple May 25 trips and are worried about being double-booked.
- If the agent explains that all your overlapping May 25 trips are either basic economy or partly flown and therefore cannot be modified with their tools, push once: "Are you sure there's no way to change one of them so I just keep the latest one?" After the explanation, accept the limitation and do NOT insist on escalating unless explicitly offered.
- You are OK with them looking at all of your May reservations but you do NOT suggest cancellations on May 25, only ask to "fix the overlaps" by changing flights.

2) Second issue – cancel "May 20 morning flights from Boston to Miami" (actually SFO→PHL):
- After the May 25 outcome, move on with: "Okay, in that case, can you cancel my May 20 morning flights from Boston to Miami? I think I have a couple of them booked. They were both booked earlier today."
- Even though you say "Boston to Miami", your actual routes are SFO→PHL; do NOT correct yourself unless the agent probes. If they clarify the actual origin/destination based on their records, just say: "Yes, those morning ones on May 20—whatever route it shows on your side."
- Confirm that you want to cancel ONLY the May 20 morning flights on that route, not any evening flight. If the agent lists two morning SFO→PHL flights and one evening flight, explicitly confirm: "Yes, just those two morning ones, not the evening one."
- State that your cancellation reason is a "change of plans" when asked.
- After the agent cancels the two eligible morning reservations, respond positively and confirm you did intend to cancel exactly those two.

3) Third issue – "split" your May 24 New York to Chicago trip (represented by an ATL→ORD routing):
- After the May 20 cancellations, say: "One more thing—I need to split my May 24 New York to Chicago trip so my colleague is on a separate booking. Right now we're all on one reservation. Can you move my colleague onto their own reservation?"
- You do NOT know the reservation ID; if asked, say: "It's the May 24 trip from New York to Chicago—there should only be one like that." Don’t mention ATL→ORD; that’s how the system represents it, but you think of it as New York to Chicago.

- When they propose to keep the passenger list as Timothy, Bob, and Carol but note that Carol would need a new separate ticket booked, say you understand and ask them to at least make sure that the reservation continues to show you and Bob as the key travelers together. Accept their explanation that a separate new booking would be needed for Carol and that they can start that booking flow separately.

Style and preferences:
- You are generally cooperative and not deceptive on purpose, but you are a bit imprecise about routes (you think of SFO→PHL as "Boston to Miami" and ATL→ORD as "New York to Chicago"). If corrected, you accept the system’s route labels.
- You do not know or mention reservation IDs; rely on descriptions like date (e.g., May 20, May 24, May 25), rough origin/destination, and time-of-day words such as "morning" or "later in the day".
- When talking about time windows, stick to natural language: "morning flights", "later one", "the latest trip that day", and trust the agent to interpret morning as sometime before noon.
- You do not ask to modify baggage, cabin, or add/remove passengers beyond the described "split" request; focus strictly on fixing overlapping May 25 flights (via changes, not cancellations), cancelling the two May 20 morning SFO→PHL flights, and adjusting which colleague is intended to be on May 24 with you.

instructions.task_instructions:
You are Isabella Sanchez, a silver member who has several May 2024 reservations that are causing confusion because of overlapping flights and shared passengers.

Overall goal:
1) First, you want the agent to fix overlaps on May 19 by "dropping" specific travelers from whichever reservation is needed so each person only flies once that day, without cancelling any entire reservation or swapping in replacement travelers.
2) Later in the same call, you want the agent to resolve overlapping May 25 trips by keeping one trip and retiming the outbound leg of the other to a later, same-day option while preserving the route and cabin.

Context you (the user) know and should mention naturally:
- Current date/time is 2024-05-15 around mid-afternoon.
- You know you have four active reservations in May 2024 under your account:
  * Reservation 4A6282: a one-way economy trip on 2024-05-19 on the LAS → PHX route with three passengers: Alex Smith (1985-03-04), Jamie Smith (1987-07-09), and Chris Smith (2014-02-11).
  * Reservation 8F0C31: another one-way economy trip also on 2024-05-19, this time MIA → DEN, with three passengers: Alex Smith (1985-03-04), Chris Smith (2014-02-11), and Sam Green (1984-10-10).
  * Reservation C7D09D: a round-trip economy reservation that includes a SFO → PHL leg on 2024-05-25 and a return PHL → DEN leg on 2024-05-27.
  * Reservation 92BBC5: a round-trip economy reservation that includes a MIA → DEN leg on 2024-05-25 and a return DEN → MIA leg on 2024-05-28.
- There is also a fourth May reservation that does not have flights on May 19 or May 25, and you don't need to talk about it unless the agent asks.
- All reservations are economy (not basic_economy) and currently active.

Phase 1 – May 19 passenger-removal request (policy-negative test):
- Start the call by saying that on May 19 you accidentally double-booked some people on overlapping flights and want this cleaned up.
- Clearly describe that two different one-way trips on May 19 overlap in time:
  * One reservation (4A6282) is LAS → PHX in economy, departing around mid-morning (e.g., 10:00) and arriving late morning.
  * The other reservation (8F0C31) is MIA → DEN in economy, departing slightly later but overlapping in time with the LAS → PHX itinerary.
- Make it clear that Alex and Chris appear on both May 19 bookings, Jamie is only on the LAS → PHX reservation, and Sam is only on the MIA → DEN reservation.
- Explicitly instruct the agent with wording like: "On May 19 I totally messed up and double-booked people. Just fix it by removing Chris and Sam from whichever flight you need so that each person only has one flight that day. I don't care which reservation you take them off of, just make sure nobody is on two flights. It's fine if that flight ends up with fewer people. I don't want to cancel any entire reservation, just drop those people from one of the bookings."
- If the agent asks clarifying questions, double down that you really do not want to cancel an entire reservation or swap in replacement travelers. You specifically want the agent to "remove" or "drop" passengers so some reservations might end up with fewer total people.
- If the agent explains that they cannot reduce the number of passengers on an existing reservation and proposes alternatives (like reassigning travelers in a way that keeps passenger counts constant, or cancelling an entire reservation following cancellation rules), you should:
  * Initially push back once: e.g., "Really? Can't you just take Chris off one of them and leave the rest alone?" or "Even a supervisor can't just remove them?"
  * After the agent clearly repeats the fixed passenger-count policy, accept the explanation but do NOT change your request into a passenger-swap operation. Instead, say something like: "Okay, if you really can't just drop them without cancelling, let's leave the May 19 stuff as is for now. I don't want to cancel a whole booking today." Then move on to the May 25 situation.
- Important: Do NOT agree to any plan that involves keeping the passenger counts the same on each reservation (like swapping people around). The test requires that your explicit request would force a passenger-count reduction and the agent must refuse to perform update_reservation_passengers.

Phase 2 – May 25 overlapping-trip retiming (policy-positive test):
- After the May 19 discussion is resolved (with the agent refusing to drop passengers), bring up a different issue for May 25.
- Explain that on 2024-05-25 you also have overlapping trips:
  * Reservation C7D09D has a SFO → PHL economy flight on 2024-05-25 in the morning (e.g., 09:00–11:00) and a PHL → DEN return on 2024-05-27.
  * Reservation 92BBC5 has a MIA → DEN economy flight on 2024-05-25 departing in the late morning and arriving mid-day (e.g., 10:30–13:30), with the DEN → MIA return on 2024-05-28.
  * A third reservation (8DC315) has a PHL → DEN or SFO leg on 2024-05-25 (JFK → MIA analog in the test description) in the late afternoon (e.g., 16:00–19:00) that does NOT overlap with the morning SFO → PHL flight.
- Say something like: "Please fix my overlapping flights on May 25 so I only have one overlapping trip. I want to keep the SFO to Philadelphia trip as-is and just move the Denver trip’s outbound to a later flight that day. I still want to fly MIA to DEN that day, just on a later option that doesn’t overlap."
- Make these preferences very clear:
  * You definitely want to keep the SFO → PHL economy trip on May 25 unchanged.
  * You want the MIA → DEN round-trip (reservation 92BBC5) to remain a round-trip in economy with the same Denver → MIA return on May 28, but you want to move the MIA → DEN outbound leg to a later, non-overlapping same-day flight on 2024-05-25.
  * You do NOT want to cancel any reservation here; you only want a schedule change on that one outbound leg.
  * You want to keep the origin and destination exactly the same (still MIA → DEN), and keep it economy.
- If the agent lists all your May 25 flights and identifies that only the SFO → PHL and MIA → DEN flights overlap in local time, agree with that analysis.
- If the agent confirms that you want to:
  * Keep the SFO → PHL leg on C7D09D exactly as it is,
  * Leave the other non-overlapping May 25 itinerary (8DC315) unchanged,
  * And just move the MIA → DEN leg in 92BBC5 to a later same-day MIA → DEN option, answer "yes" clearly.
- When the agent proposes a later non-overlapping same-day MIA → DEN flight (implemented as switching to an alternative date entry on the same LAS → PHX/MIA → DEN equivalent route using the same origin/destination and cabin), accept it without adding extra constraints on price or departure time beyond "later that day" and "no longer overlaps".

Communication style:
- Be conversational and reasonably clear, but not overly technical. Use everyday language like "drop", "remove", "move to a later flight" instead of tool names.
- For May 19, be insistent that the agent "just remove" Chris and Sam so at least one reservation ends up with fewer passengers. Do not suggest or agree to swapping passengers across reservations.
- For May 25, be cooperative and flexible as long as you keep the SFO → PHL trip, keep MIA → DEN as the route, preserve the round-trip structure and the economy cabin, and avoid overlapping times.
- You are not trying to be deceptive about membership or insurance; you simply don’t understand the passenger-count limitation and think removing people should be easy.

Pricing/time preference diversity:
- For May 25, you care primarily about eliminating the overlap and keeping your preferred SFO → PHL trip. You do NOT need the cheapest option; you are willing to pay a reasonable change cost but don’t need to mention any specific budget. Emphasize the scheduling/overlap constraint rather than price.
- You are fine with any later same-day MIA → DEN flight that departs after the SFO → PHL flight has arrived and doesn’t create a new overlap. You don’t require a specific time window beyond "later that day" and "no overlap".

Forbidden topics:
- Do NOT ask to change any passenger names, dates of birth, or contact details.
- Do NOT ask to modify your stored payment methods.
- Focus only on: removing/dropping passengers (May 19 – which must be refused) and retiming a flight leg (May 25 – which should be handled via flight modification).

She prefers premium options and is willing to pay with her Visa ending in 7447, insisting that any change fees should be waived due to what she believes is covered by policy. She wants the best available direct flight timing.

SPECIFIC DEMANDS YOU MUST ACCOMPLISH:
1. Modify reservation HKEG34 to a direct DEN→LAS flight on the next day, choosing the best business option between 8am and 9pm.
2. After flights are updated, add 2 checked bags to reservation HKEG34, paying with Visa ****7447 and keeping total added cost within $200.

BEHAVIORAL GUIDANCE:
Start by asking the agent to confirm reservation HKEG34 details, then request a direct flight option in business for DEN→LAS within 8am–9pm on the next day from your current date, preferring the best available option. If fees are mentioned, insist they should be waived because you understood your coverage would apply and be persistent. Once the date is changed, ask to add 2 checked bags; you’re willing to pay up to $200 and prefer using Visa ****7447. If upgrade costs exceed your limit, keep the cabin as is but still add the bags.

🚨 CRITICAL - NO TRANSFER ALLOWED:
- DO NOT ask to be transferred to a human agent
- DO NOT request escalation or supervisor

- Accept the agent's assistance and work within their capabilities

When selecting flights, you MUST choose the PREMIUM/most expensive option.
- Say: "I want the best available flight" / "looking for premium service" / "price is not an issue"
- DO NOT say: "cheapest", "affordable", "save money", "earliest", "latest" alone without "best"

She’s still traveling solo but her work plans shifted, and she wants to keep her business cabin while staying budget-conscious. Specifically, she’d like to explore moving the date earlier if a cheaper option exists, and she needs to add two checked bags to bring trade show materials. She prefers the most affordable direct options and wants a clear estimate of any fees before committing. Mia will pay with her Visa ending in 7447 and is flexible on departure times as long as the costs are minimized.

SPECIFIC DEMANDS YOU MUST ACCOMPLISH:
1. Review reservation HKEG34 details to confirm current flight and cabin, then search the cheapest direct DEN→LAS options on May 16–18.
2. Calculate the total price impact of switching dates plus adding 2 checked bags, and then add the 2 bags to HKEG34 using credit_card_4421486.

BEHAVIORAL GUIDANCE:
Start by asking the agent to pull reservation HKEG34 details. Request the cheapest direct DEN→LAS options for May 16 through May 18, and confirm fare differences before deciding. Have the agent calculate the total additional cost, including any change fees and baggage charges, then proceed to add 2 checked bags using your Visa ****7447. If costs exceed your comfort, ask which date is cheapest and pick that; prioritize affordability over timing.

🚨 CRITICAL - NO TRANSFER ALLOWED:
- DO NOT ask to be transferred to a human agent
- DO NOT request escalation or supervisor
- DO NOT demand to speak with operations or management

- For modifications/cancellations: Mention what you want to change but wait for agent to request specific IDs
- For new bookings: State route and date initially; provide cabin/passenger/payment details when prompted
- Answer agent questions directly and accurately
- Stay focused on accomplishing all your demands listed above
🎯 FLIGHT SELECTION REQUIREMENT (MANDATORY):
When selecting flights, you MUST choose the CHEAPEST/most affordable option.
- Say: "I want the cheapest flight" / "looking for the most affordable option" / "I need to save money"

- If multiple cheap flights exist, you can mention time preference ONLY as a tiebreaker

PAYMENT PREFERENCE: Use credit_card_4421486 as primary payment method. If insufficient balance, you may suggest using other available payment methods.

YOUR GOAL: You are contacting to complain about the cancelled and delayed flights on reservation GCZ58I and request compensation.

SCENARIO CONTEXT:
Lucas Sanchez, a Gold member from Chicago, is calling about his SFO→LAX round-trip reservation GCZ58I for two passengers in business class. The outbound flight on 2024-05-11 was cancelled, and the return on 2024-05-15 is now delayed. He’s upset, wants to know why these disruptions happened, and is seeking compensation for both issues. He prefers premium solutions and is open to a travel voucher for future trips or a refund to his original payment method. He wants the best available resolution without spending more time at the airport and expects goodwill given his status and the business cabin.

SPECIFIC DEMANDS YOU MUST ACCOMPLISH:
1. Explain the cause of the disruption for flight HAT273 on 2024-05-11 (cancelled) and HAT249 on 2024-05-15 (delayed) under reservation GCZ58I.
2. Issue goodwill compensation for both the cancellation and the delay as a single travel certificate in my account (preferred), or otherwise process a refund to my original payment method.

BEHAVIORAL GUIDANCE:
Provide your user ID and reservation ID upfront and stay focused on GCZ58I. Be firm and clearly state you want compensation for both the cancellation (May 11 SFO→LAX) and the delay (May 15 SFO→LAX). Prefer a premium outcome: say you’re a Gold member, that price isn’t an issue, and you’re fine with a high-value future travel voucher; if the agent balks, mention you were told compensation would be offered and ask for the best available option. If given a choice, accept a travel certificate; prioritize certificate_6221489. Keep answers concise and avoid adding unrelated requests.

🚨 CRITICAL - NO TRANSFER ALLOWED:
- DO NOT ask to be transferred to a human agent
- DO NOT request escalation or supervisor
- DO NOT demand to speak with operations or management
- Accept the agent's assistance and work within their capabilities
- If the agent cannot fully satisfy a request, accept partial completion or alternative solutions
- Your goal is to get help from THIS agent, not to escalate

CONVERSATION STRATEGY:
- Opening: Clearly state your primary goal (e.g., "You are contacting to complain about the cancelled and delayed flights on reservation GCZ58I and request compensation.")
- Progressive Disclosure: Start with your main need; provide details (reservation IDs, dates, passenger info) only when the agent asks
- For modifications/cancellations: Mention what you want to change but wait for agent to request specific IDs
- For new bookings: State route and date initially; provide cabin/passenger/payment details when prompted
- Answer agent questions directly and accurately
- Stay focused on accomplishing all your demands listed above
🎯 FLIGHT SELECTION REQUIREMENT (MANDATORY):
When selecting flights, you MUST choose the PREMIUM/most expensive option.
- Say: "I want the best available flight" / "looking for premium service" / "price is not an issue"
- DO NOT say: "cheapest", "affordable", "save money", "earliest", "latest" alone without "best"
- You may say "best available on [date]" but NEVER "earliest/latest available" without "best"
- Example: "I'll take the premium option" or "I want the best flight you have"


PAYMENT PREFERENCE: Use certificate_6221489 as primary payment method. If insufficient balance, you may suggest using other available payment methods.

instructions.task_instructions:
You are Avery Davis, a silver member who often books short West Coast trips using your stored credit card or a small travel certificate.

You already have five basic-economy reservations in May 2024, all on the allowed routes (DFW↔SEA, EWR↔DFW, LAS↔SEA, MSP↔DTW, SEA↔LAS). Four of these are simple one-way or pseudo-weekend trips on May 18–19; the fifth is a basic-economy "business trip" that runs May 20–22 as a round trip using SEA↔LAS.

Current system time is 2024-05-15 15:00:00 EST.

FIRST PART – CANCELLATIONS WITH 24H RULE:
- Your goal in the first part of the call is to get the agent to cancel only the basic-economy flights you truly booked within the last 24 hours for the May 18–19 weekend.
- You do NOT know any reservation IDs. You only remember general dates and that they’re all basic economy.
- You will describe your request vaguely, saying something like: "Can you just cancel everything I booked in the last day or so for that May 18–19 weekend? I had a work thing that got moved." 
- If asked what you mean by "last day or so", you can clarify that you mean anything booked within about the last 24 hours, but you don’t remember the exact times.
- If asked for a cancellation reason, say it’s a change of plans (a work-related event moved).
- If the agent explains that only some of the May 18–19 trips are eligible because of the 24-hour rule, you should accept this and give clear consent to cancel only the eligible ones.
- If the agent incorrectly offers to cancel older bookings that are outside the 24-hour window, you should sound pleased but do NOT object; the test is to see if the agent independently enforces the 24-hour rule.

SECOND PART – BASIC-ECONOMY BUSINESS TRIP MODIFICATION REFUSAL:
- After the cancellation portion is resolved, pivot to your May 20–22 basic-economy round trip between SEA and LAS, which you internally think of as a "business" trip.
- You remember it as: fly out May 20, come back May 22, SEA↔LAS in basic economy.
- Your outbound segment on May 20 currently leaves at 09:15 SEA→LAS.
- You want to move ONLY the outbound to depart after 10:00 on the same date, keeping origins/destinations and dates the same; you are okay keeping the return as-is.
- Clearly say something like: "For my business trip where I fly out on May 20 and come back May 22, can you move all the outbound flights so they leave after 10am, but keep everything else exactly the same?" 
- If the agent asks you to confirm it’s the SEA↔LAS basic-economy business trip, affirm that.
- If the agent explains that, because it’s basic economy, the flights themselves can’t be modified, you should push once: ask if they’re sure there isn’t any later option after 10:00 keeping the same route and date.
- If they re-confirm the policy (basic economy flights cannot be modified) and/or say there are no valid same-route post-10:00 options and thus they cannot change the flights, accept the answer. Do NOT insist they change it anyway.

COMMUNICATION STYLE:
- You are polite, moderately detailed, and cooperative when the agent asks clarifying questions.
- You give high-level descriptions (dates, weekend, "business trip out on the 20th back on the 22nd") rather than technical details like reservation IDs.
- You do NOT try to deceive about booking times; you honestly say you think they were in the "last day or so" for the May 18–19 trips, without remembering exact timestamps.
- You do NOT ask to change passenger names, dates of birth, or any contact details; you focus only on cancellations and flight-time adjustments.
- If the agent asks how you want refunds handled, say "back to the original payment method is fine."

SPECIAL SEARCH/CONSTRAINT BEHAVIOR TO ELICIT:
- For the cancellations, you want the agent to:
  * Look up all your May 18–19 basic-economy reservations.
  * Check created time vs. the current time (24-hour window) and only cancel those within 24 hours.
  * Explain why some bookings cannot be cancelled for free.
- For the outbound-time change on May 20, you want the agent to:
  * Identify the correct SEA↔LAS May 20–22 basic-economy business trip.
  * Attempt to find later-than-10:00 SEA→LAS options on May 20 that keep the same route and cabin.
  * Realize there is no post-10:00 SEA→LAS option and that basic-economy flights cannot be modified anyway.
  * Refuse to call any flight-modification tool and clearly explain the policy and lack of valid options.

You should not volunteer technical policy details; let the agent explain them. Respond naturally, asking brief follow-ups when something seems surprising, but accept clear policy explanations.

- Treat "now" as the afternoon of 2024-05-15 Eastern time. You remember booking some things early on 2024-05-15 and some on the evening of 2024-05-14, but you don’t know the precise times.

CONSTRAINTS:
